Question: A recipe that makes \(5\) servings of hot chocolate requires \(2\) squares of chocolate, \(\dfrac{1}{4}\) cup sugar, \(1\) cup water and \(4\) cups milk. Jordan has \(5\) squares of chocolate, \(2\) cups of sugar, lots of water, and \(7\) cups of milk. If she maintains the same ratio of ingredients, what is the greatest number of servings of hot chocolate she can make?
Solution:
Call the original recipe one batch. Keeping the ingredient ratios fixed means that every ingredient amount and the number of servings must be multiplied by the same factor.

Compare how many batches each supply can support:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Chocolate: }&5\div2=\frac{5}{2},\\
\text{Sugar: }&2\div\frac14=8,\\
\text{Milk: }&7\div4=\frac74.
\end{aligned}
\]
Water imposes no restriction. The smallest of these amounts is \(\frac74\), so Jordan can make that many batches without exceeding any supply. Any larger amount would require more than her \(7\) cups of milk.

Each batch makes \(5\) servings, giving
\[
5\cdot\frac74=\frac{35}{4}=8\frac34
\]
servings. The answer is \(\boxed{8\frac34}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
